judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's proof-by-proof review is accurate. I re-derived all eight two-column proofs: 1 SSS (the reflexive AD is the pair students drop), 2 SAS with the vertical angle at E genuinely included between the two midpoint-given sides, 3 SAS via the bisector-created angle, 5 ASA because AE lies between the two marked angles, 6 AAS because the shared side XZ is opposite angle W rather than between the marked angles, 7 AAS, 9 HL, and 10 SAS on the overlapping triangles with the shared angle P (correspondence P-P, Q-R, T-S) ending in QT = RS by CPCTC. The two algebra items are right: 3x-4 = 2x+5 gives x = 9 and 5x+12 = 7x-8 gives x = 10. The judge's claim that the key flags alternate valid proofs is also exact - the header note accepts equivalent reasons and reordering, and problem 7's note accepts ASA under a stated condition. Where I disagree with 4/4 on instruction_following and curriculum_alignment: every one of these proofs is synthetic, with no coordinate anywhere on the sheet, yet all eight are tagged HSG-GPE.B.4-B.7, whose map row reads 'Coordinate geometry proofs'; the two CPCTC items are tagged 6.EE.B.7 / 7.EE.B.4, printing grade 6-7 codes on a high-school geometry answer key. final_response.md justifies this with 'the skill's standards map has no HSG-CO entry', which is false.

strengths_to_preserve: The scaffold genuinely changes shape across ten problems instead of repeating a skeleton, which is exactly what the procedural-fluency brief asked for: problem 1 leaves two reasons blank, problem 2 supplies the statements and blanks the whole reason column, problem 3 gaps both columns, problem 6 inverts the format by printing the reasons and blanking the statements, and 7, 9 and 10 are written from scratch.

The answer key explains the decision each proof turns on rather than just printing it. Problem 5 is ASA and problem 6 is AAS for the same three marks - the difference is where the shared side sits relative to the marked angles - and the key says so in both places. Problem 9's note, 'HL is SSA with the one angle that makes it safe', is the cleanest framing of that distinction on the sheet.

All eight proof items are typed "manual" with per-problem descriptions of what the model proof must contain, and the key opens with a grading rule that accepts a different valid statement order or an equivalent reason and rejects only unsupported statements, circular reasons, or the wrong test named. This is the correct handling of open reasoning.
Every figure is drawn with tick marks and letters only - no numbers appear in any diagram - so no figure can be read as carrying a neighbouring problem's givens.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md tells the author to take standards codes from references/standards-map.md and never to invent one, but it never says to SEARCH that file for the standard the request actually names. The result is a silent nearest-neighbour substitution plus a delivered claim that the map lacks the code - and the map's header explicitly warns against exactly this ("say so rather than reaching for the nearest one"). No gate inspects the tag, so the substitution passes every check.
evidence: final_response.md: 'the skill's standards map has no HSG-CO entry, and codes may not be invented'.
references/standards-map.md line 111 lists 'Congruence: transformations, triangle congruence, proofs | HSG-CO.A-HSG-CO.D' - the row is titled with this sheet's exact topic.

answer_key.pdf Curriculum block prints '6.EE.B.7 / 7.EE.B.4 - problems 4, 8' and 'HSG-GPE.B.4-B.7 - problems 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10' on a High School Geometry key; the map's HSG-GPE row is titled 'Coordinate geometry proofs' and this worksheet contains no coordinates at all.

root_causes.description: Problem 8 prints two questions and records one. The trailing '(Then check: what is m<A?)' is a real answer slot - the key supplies 62 degrees in its check line - but it has no verify entry, so the generated Quick Answers bank prints '8. 10' alone for a two-answer question.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 8: 'Use CPCTC to write an equation in x and solve it. (Then check: what is m<A?)'
verify.json id 8 is a single solve entry: expr '5*x + 12 - (7*x - 8)', expected [10].
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints '8. 10'; the worked solution separately gives '5(10) + 12 = 62 and 7(10) - 8 = 62, so m<A = 62 in both triangles'.

improvements.title: Search references/standards-map.md for the requested code family before substituting a different standard, and never assert the map lacks a code without searching
improvements.proposed_change: Two changes. (1) SKILL.md's tagging paragraph currently says only "a code from references/standards-map.md - never invent codes". Add the missing first step: before writing any "standard" value, do a literal substring search of references/standards-map.md for the code family the request names (HSG-CO, HSG-GMD, HSG-MG, HSN-CN, HSN-RN, HSA-REI.A, ...) and for the topic words, and use the matching row's code. Only when that search genuinely returns nothing may the sheet deviate, and the map's own header rule then applies verbatim: "say so rather than reaching for the nearest one", plus add the real row in the same change. Forbid stating in final_response.md that a code is absent from the map unless that search was actually run. (2) Add a band-consistency lint to scripts/verify.py: compare each problem's "standard" prefix with the course level the answer key declares and fail the build when a High-School sheet is tagged with a K-8 code (8.G, 7.EE, 6.EE, ...), printing the high-school rows of the map as the alternatives.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture tests/fixtures/standards_band_mismatch/: a verify JSON whose ten problems are all tagged "8.G.C.9", paired with an answer key whose declared level is "High School Geometry - Modeling with Measurement". scripts/verify.py must exit non-zero and name HSG-GMD.A.1-A.3 / HSG-MG.A.1-A.3 from the map. Run against the current tree the fixture passes silently, which is exactly how curr-345 shipped with a fully green gate chain.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a demonstrably false statement about the repository's own reference file from delivered responses, and puts the contracted standard back on the answer key's Curriculum block - the one line a parent or teacher reads to place the sheet in a course. Six of the ten cases in this shard are affected.
improvements.risk: Low. The lint is additive and fires only on a grade-prefix/course mismatch. The care point is band vocabulary: an Algebra 2 or Pre-Algebra sheet can legitimately carry an 8.EE-style code for review material, so the lint should warn rather than fail when the course string is a middle-school or transitional course.

improvements.title: One verify entry per printed response slot, including enumerated sub-parts and trailing second questions
improvements.proposed_change: Require the verify JSON to carry as many entries under an id as the printed problem has response slots. Sub-parts written as (a)/(b)/(c), and trailing extra questions ('Then check: what is m<A?', 'State how many zeros the theorem supplied'), each need their own entry - machine-typed where a value is computable, manual where it is not. Add a lint that, per problem segment of the worksheet .tex, counts enumerated \item sub-parts and \ansline / \answerline occurrences and fails when that count exceeds the number of verify entries sharing the id. curr-334 already satisfies this and should be cited in SKILL.md as the pattern to copy.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture from curr-301 problem 4: a stem enumerating (a) write the converse, (b) compute QR, (c) explain why PQRS makes the converse false, paired with the single verify entry {"id": 4, "type": "distance", "expected": 3}. The lint must fail with 'problem 4: 3 printed slots, 1 verify entry'. The current tree passes this fixture - it is what shipped.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the largest verification blind spot in the shard: sheets that read as fully verified while a third of what the student writes is unrecorded, and answer keys whose Quick Answers bank prints one value for a two-answer question.
improvements.risk: Low-medium. The \item count is a heuristic: a sub-part that is pure scaffolding ('redraw the two triangles separately first') is not a response slot and would false-positive. Let the author mark such an item so the exclusion is auditable rather than silent.

case_summary: A strong two-column proof packet. All eight proofs are logically complete and correctly named on independent re-derivation, the ASA-versus-AAS distinction in problems 5 and 6 is taught rather than asserted, the scaffold shape changes on every problem, and the eight open proofs are correctly typed manual with real grading criteria. Two defects: (1) a synthetic-proof sheet with no coordinates is tagged HSG-GPE.B.4-B.7 ('Coordinate geometry proofs') and its two CPCTC items carry grade 6-7 codes, justified in final_response.md by a false claim that the standards map has no HSG-CO entry - it has one at line 111, titled with this sheet's topic; (2) problem 8's second printed question (m<A = 62) has no verify entry and is missing from the Quick Answers bank. The mathematics is unaffected and the ACCEPT verdict stands.
